text:
Tessa Morgan: Dropping latest Console mockups for “Security → Audit Export” (destination list + create flow + destination detail). Figma: https://figma.com/file/ri-audit-export/console-mockups?node-id=1842%3A991 :eyes:

Tessa Morgan: Main things I want feedback on today:
- health states + what we show in the header (Healthy / Degraded / Paused)
- how filters are expressed (include/exclude, chips vs textarea)
- error presentation (copy, surfacing error_id, links to docs)

Chloe Martin: :eyes: looking now

Felix Schneider: thanks — quick Q: do we want “Paused” to be a health state or separate badge (operational state vs health)? Right now API has enabled/paused + degraded as computed.

Tessa Morgan: good call. In mockups, I treated Paused as a “status pill” and still show “Health: —” but it felt weird.

Sean Gallagher: From on-call POV I’d rather Console show something that maps 1:1 to our state machine. Operators will ask “is it paused or broken?”

Naomi Feldman: +1 to being explicit. For beta we need clear customer language: Paused (you did it) vs Degraded (we’re failing deliveries) vs Healthy.

Svetlana Petrenko: Agree. Also: “Paused” isn’t “healthy” but it’s not “degraded” either. Maybe top of page has two lines:
- State: Enabled | Paused
- Health (when enabled): Healthy | Degraded

Tessa Morgan: I can adjust. So if Paused we show State=Paused and hide health widget / show “No events will be delivered while paused”.

Marcus Lin: Please avoid “No events will be delivered” without nuance — we buffer. Might be “Delivery is stopped; events may continue to buffer until you resume (subject to retention/backlog limits)”.

Kevin Osei: +1. Also we should remind at-least-once + potential duplicates somewhere, but maybe not in the health header.

Chloe Martin: On the detail page, I like the “Last delivered” + “Backlog estimate” card. Can we also show “Last attempted” even if failed? Helps debugging.

Felix Schneider: API can provide last_success_at + last_attempt_at + last_error. Backlog estimate is computed from queue depth + checkpoint lag. We can add fields.

Tessa Morgan: Nice. In mockup I have:
- Last delivered
- Delivery latency p95 (24h)
- Backlog estimate
- Last error
Maybe we swap latency for last_attempt? (or make latency a mini chart)

Sean Gallagher: latency p95 is useful but might be too much for beta UI. I’d prioritize “last_attempt” + “last_error” + link to docs/runbook.

Naomi Feldman: For customer experience: keep it simple. “Healthy / Degraded” plus “Last delivered” and “Last error (with error ID)” covers most.

Kira Thompson: From docs perspective, if we standardize error IDs, we can have “Search docs for this error” or “Contact support with error ID”. But we need consistent copy.

Svetlana Petrenko: Re: error copy — can we avoid raw connector messages? Splunk/Datadog return weird stuff sometimes.

Felix Schneider: we’ll map to a small taxonomy (AUTH, THROTTLE, SCHEMA, NETWORK, UNKNOWN). Under it can show truncated raw message behind “View details”.

Marcus Lin: Please ensure raw details don’t leak secrets (tokens, HEC URL with embedded creds). Redaction required.

Tessa Morgan: Filter UX: right now it’s a builder with 3 sections:
1) Event types (multi-select)
2) Actor (service/user) includes/excludes
3) Environment (prod/staging)
Plus “Advanced: IP / region” behind toggle.

Chloe Martin: I like the builder but we need validation feedback. What happens if they select contradictory include+exclude? (e.g. include event_type=login and exclude event_type=login)

Svetlana Petrenko: In DES-612 we talked about inline errors + preventing save. Maybe show a “Rule summary” string at top so they can understand what they’re creating.

Tessa Morgan: mockups include a summary line:
“Export events where event_type in [auth.login, api_key.rotate] AND environment=prod; exclude actor_type=service”

Naomi Feldman: Summary helps a lot for security reviews.

Kevin Osei: For schema v1 we’ll probably have ~30 event types. Can we group them? Auth / RBAC / Keys / Export config / Billing(?) etc.

Tessa Morgan: yup, event types are grouped in the dropdown. Also added “Search” within event types.

Felix Schneider: Implementation note: filter DSL supports include/exclude lists, but no arbitrary boolean expressions in beta. So UI should avoid implying “OR groups”.

Tessa Morgan: good catch — I’ll remove the “Add group” affordance I had in one screen.

Sean Gallagher: Another UX idea: “Test filter” button that shows “Matched last 50 audit events” (from stored sample). But might be too much.

Chloe Martin: We already have “Send test event” for destination creds. Maybe separate:
- “Send test event” (synthetic)
- “Preview filter” (shows which event types would pass)
Preview could just be static, not needing event store.

Felix Schneider: preview can be “validate only” + show computed rule summary; no event store dependency.

Marcus Lin: For “Send test event”, ensure it’s labeled as synthetic and not confused with real audit events. Also the test event itself should be audited (config change + test sent).

Naomi Feldman: yes please: audit log of “audit_export.test_sent” event_type.

Tessa Morgan: Health states in list view: I currently show each destination row with
- Destination name + sink icon
- State pill
- Health dot
- Last delivered time
- “Manage”
Any objections?

Svetlana Petrenko: List view should also show if misconfigured (e.g., missing creds). Otherwise customer will keep clicking in.

Felix Schneider: we can show “Needs attention” when validation fails / secret missing.

Sean Gallagher: “Needs attention” should page? (jk). But yeah show a distinct state for “misconfigured” separate from “degraded due to delivery failures”.

Tessa Morgan: I’ll add “Configuration: Invalid” banner on detail page when validation fails, and list view badge.

Kira Thompson: Copy suggestion:
- “Configuration error” (with what to fix)
- “Delivery degraded” (with next steps)
- “Paused” (with resume CTA)
Also please link to setup guides (Splunk / Datadog / S3) contextually.

Chloe Martin: +1. Destination detail page could have right rail “Resources” with links:
- Setup guide for sink type
- Dedupe guidance
- Replay tooling (if enabled)
- Contact support

Kevin Osei: Don’t link replay to customers until safeguards are in. Maybe keep “Replay” behind separate permission/flag.

Felix Schneider: replay endpoint will be RBAC-gated + behind feature flag for beta. UI can hide.

Marcus Lin: RBAC: only Workspace Owner + Security Admin should see “Audit Export”. Please ensure we don’t leak destination URLs to read-only roles.

Chloe Martin: we have new permission gate in progress. Will align with Security Admin role.

Tessa Morgan: Great. Action items from me:
- Split “State” vs “Health” in header and list
- Adjust paused copy re: buffering
- Simplify health card to: last_delivered, last_attempted, last_error (+ error_id)
- Remove “Add group” from filter builder, keep beta DSL constraints
- Add config invalid banner + list badge

Tessa Morgan: If anyone has strong opinions on the Degraded UI: right now it’s yellow banner with “Delivery issues detected” + “View details”. Would you prefer red?

Sean Gallagher: Use red only for “Delivery stopped” (hard failure) maybe. Yellow for transient (throttling). But that requires classification.

Felix Schneider: we do have error taxonomy. Could set severity mapping: AUTH/SCHEMA = red (won’t self-heal), THROTTLE/NETWORK = yellow (may self-heal).

Naomi Feldman: Love that. Customers care about “needs action” vs “monitoring”.

Tessa Morgan: ok I’ll revise banners based on severity + add “Recommended action” line.

Chloe Martin: :thumbsup: once updated, tag me on node so I can sanity check vs what backend can return.

Tessa Morgan: will do — thanks all
